solutionSql: SELECT d.id, d.name, s.name AS supervisor_name FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN drivers AS s ON s.id = d.supervisor_id ORDER BY d.id;

rules.howSolved: LEFT JOIN from drivers so a driver with no supervisor (NULL supervisor_id) is kept.
drivers is joined a second time as s, matching s.id to d.supervisor_id, so supervisor_name is the supervisor's name.
The missing supervisor comes from the outer join and is NULL; no empty string is produced.

ambiguities: The instructions do not say what happens if a supervisor_id matches no driver; the LEFT JOIN returns NULL there, which fits 'missing'. The schema declares supervisor_id as a foreign key, so this should not arise.
